term: lending descent, chain, regress and circle
definition: Descent m I e D says e is in D, each member occurs and has an actual lender, and D is a #734 Trap for I over the actually lending records. Chain m P e f is a sequence from e through events satisfying P, each next event a contributor of an actual lender of the previous one. Regress is such a chain that is injective; Circle is one that revisits an event.
note: Analyst structure. A Chain follows one contributor per step, while Supply needs all contributors of a record; a Regress or Circle alone is not asserted to be a Descent. No clause says a descent is impossible, and the fork does not select a branch. DEF-DERIVATIVE-JOINT-SUPPLY gives the Trap it reuses.
